about: Sixteen cards written 2026-11-27 by a Claude session following tools/combo-cards/BRIEF.md, most-used missing pairs first: psyche emotion centers with the childhood or twenties aura beside them, and childhood aura with twenties aura, inner and outer psyche chart.

cards.position: As a child they lived in a big inner world of imagination, could not hurt a fly, and escaped into themselves when threatened (7). The emotional response that settled from it is fire: push, hold the feeling down, and be hard on themselves (9).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 7 drifts off and watches (7). 9 gets up and does (9).

course.text: "A parent or sibling may have passed away, leaving an inner feeling that life was difficult and you had to fend for yourself."

reasoning: A child left to manage alone (7) grows a voice that says "then be strong" (9).
They are hard on the dreamer they once were (9): daydreaming (7) now feels like wasted time.
The same passage says the need to fend for oneself gave inner strength (9) and a strong intuition (7) that can be used to lead and guide others.
cards.best: Kept the child's compassion (7) and added the strength to act on it (9).
cards.worst: Escapes into their own head (7) and then punishes themselves for it (9).

cards.position: As a child they lived in a big inner world of imagination and escaped into themselves when threatened (7). In their twenties they were very sensitive: easily hurt, slow to speak out, with others stepping over their limits (11/2).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are receptive, inward numbers with no armor (7, 11/2). The escape into an inner world is doubled.

course.about: 11/2 and 7 together in a center (written for the name chart's mind center)
course.text: "create a lot of mental instability and feeling of vulnerability."

reasoning: The child escaped inward (7), and the young adult did the same when people overstepped (11/2).
The child could not hurt a fly (7). The young adult could not say no (11/2).
What it leaves them with is rare: a child's imagination (7) and a grown feel for what others are going through (11/2).
cards.best: Imagines what another person is feeling (7) and is nearly always right (11/2).
cards.worst: Zoned out as a child (7) and let people walk over them later (11/2).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 9, a harsh voice toward themselves.

cards.position: By nature the child in them is original and a bit odd, the black sheep who either withdraws or rebels (13/4). The emotional response that goes with it is to turn things over in the head and feel misunderstood (12/3).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both feel shut out: 13/4 as the outsider (13/4), 12/3 as the one wronged (12/3). It is doubled.

course.about: a 13/4 childhood aura with 12/3 in the psyche chart's emotion center
course.text: "although you have access to a great deal of imagination and originality on the inside, and may sometimes feel like a victim on the inside (solar plexus 12/3), you seem more "normal" and restrained on the outside."

reasoning: By nature they see things their own way (13/4) and feel alone in it (12/3).
The combo guide's phrase for 12/3 beside a 4 is the black sheep: here it is said twice (13/4, 12/3).
They hide how different they are (13/4), which guarantees that nobody understands them (12/3).
cards.best: Has an original mind (13/4) and the patience to work an idea out fully (12/3).
cards.worst: Feels like an outcast (13/4) and reads every look as proof of it (12/3).

cards.position: By nature the child in them is original and a bit odd, the black sheep who either withdraws or rebels (13/4). By nature their twenties side is strong, cautious and in control, with nobody let too close (8).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: The one thing both agree on is "I'm on my own" (13/4, 8). Apart: 13/4 breaks the rules, 8 keeps them.

course.about: a 13/4 childhood aura with an 8 beside it
course.text: "With psychic life expression 8, you can remember everything because the number 8 stands for memory and karma. You especially remember all the times you felt different, unwanted and like the black sheep."

reasoning: The child was pushed out (13/4). The twenties side makes sure it cannot happen again, by controlling who comes near (8).
The same passage: standing up for themselves comes across as harsh, even territorial (8), because a small provocation recalls the old feeling (13/4).
The combo guide says 4 and 8 fight. In this pair the wild child (13/4) is held down by the careful adult (8).
cards.best: Stands up for people who are left out (8) because they remember being one (13/4).
cards.worst: Remembers every time they were made to feel odd (13/4) and forgives none of it (8).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 12/3, overthinking and feeling misunderstood.

phrases: Charmer by Nature, Fighter at Heart
cards.position: By nature the child in them is charming, a little flirtatious, and knows how to get its way (15/6). The emotional response that goes with it is fire: push on, and be hard on themselves (9).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 15/6 wins by being liked (15/6). 9 wins by being stronger (9).

course.text: "There's definitely a great ability to make things happen from behind the scenes by pulling the right strings."

reasoning: By nature they try charm first (15/6) and force second (9), and usually one of them works.
They want to be adored (15/6) and scold themselves for wanting it (9).
The combo guide: when 15/6 stands with a power number such as 9, no effort is spared to get things their way.
cards.best: Gets people on their side (15/6) and then gets the job done (9).
cards.worst: Pulls strings behind the scenes (15/6) and turns angry when caught (9).

cards.position: By nature the child in them is charming, a little flirtatious, and knows how to get its way (15/6). By nature their twenties side is expansive and mentally awake, and often feels misunderstood by people (12/3).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 15/6 knows how to be liked (15/6). 12/3 feels that it is not (12/3).

course.about: the combo guide on 15/6 beside unbalanced numbers such as 12/3
course.text: "The unbalanced numbers can bring out the worst in the number 15/6, so that emotions take over"

reasoning: By nature they charm people (15/6) and then suspect they were liked only for the charm (12/3).
The child's gossip (15/6) comes back in their twenties as being talked about (12/3).
The combo guide ties 12/3 with 15/6 to paranoia, drama and addiction: strong feeling (15/6) with a head that reads it wrongly (12/3).
cards.best: Draws people in (15/6) and gives them something to think about (12/3).
cards.worst: Stirs up drama (15/6) and then feels like its victim (12/3).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 9, a harsh voice toward themselves.

cards.position: By nature the child in them is a fighter: fair, direct, and guarded about showing feeling (9). The emotional response that goes with it is attraction: charm, wanting to be wanted, and drama (15/6).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 9 keeps people at arm's length (9). 15/6 wants them close (15/6).

course.text: "You will typically seek attention because of 15/6 and become very angry (9) if others take it (9) and may find it difficult to feel rejected."

reasoning: By nature they act as if they need nobody (9), while needing very much to be wanted (15/6).
A fighter does not ask (9), so the wish for affection (15/6) comes out sideways: as teasing, testing, a scene.
Being turned down is felt as losing a fight (9), on top of the hurt itself (15/6).
cards.best: Protects fiercely (9) whoever they have given their heart to (15/6).
cards.worst: Pushes a person away (9) to see whether they will come back (15/6).

cards.position: By nature their twenties side is strong, cautious and in control, with nobody let too close (8). The emotional response under it is attraction: charm, wanting to be wanted, and drama (15/6).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 8 is duty and distance (8). 15/6 is desire and closeness (15/6). Lecture: 6 likes 8.

course.about: the combo guide on 15/6 with 8, at the more balanced end
course.text: "someone who is good at seeing through others (15/6), but may use this to their own advantage and gain power through manipulation."

reasoning: By nature they watch people from a safe distance (8) and feel strongly drawn to them all the same (15/6).
They know what someone wants (15/6) and when to use it (8).
The guard exists (8) because the feelings behind it are so strong (15/6).
cards.best: Understands what moves a person (15/6) and uses it responsibly (8).
cards.worst: Reads someone's longing (15/6) and uses it to control them (8).

cards.position: By nature the child in them lives in a big inner world of imagination, gentle with every creature, escaping inward when threatened (7). The emotional response that goes with it is attraction: charm, wanting to be wanted, and drama (15/6).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are loved, feminine numbers (7, 15/6). The combo guide says a 7 lifts 15/6 into something hypnotic and spiritual.

course.about: 15/6 with a 7 (written for the name chart)
course.text: "a strong and hypnotic charisma that fascinates people and gives an aura of sensuality and mystery."

reasoning: By nature they do not chase (7), which makes the pull stronger (15/6).
The gentle child (7) keeps the charm (15/6) from turning into a game.
Under strong attraction (15/6) they make the other person into a dream (7), and are let down by the real one.
cards.best: Loves with imagination (7) and with passion (15/6).
cards.worst: Falls for a fantasy of someone (7) and makes a drama of the disappointment (15/6).

cards.position: By nature the child in them lives in a big inner world of imagination and escapes inward when threatened (7). By nature their twenties side is strong, cautious and in control, with nobody let too close (8).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both keep their distance and observe: the child from inside its own world (7), the young adult from behind a guard (8).

course.about: an 8 aura with a 7 beside it (written for the name chart)
course.text: "strong intuition and deep knowledge ... great success as the 8 grounds the spirituality and insight of the 7."

reasoning: The child had no defence but to drift off (7). The twenties side builds one: control (8).
Both watch before they act (7, 8), so little escapes them.
The psyche aura texts call 7 with 8 part of the "spotlight" combination: a private nature (7) that keeps getting noticed (8).
cards.best: Senses what is going on (7) and organizes around it (8).
cards.worst: Trusts nobody (8) and retreats into their own head (7).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 15/6, charm and wanting to be wanted.

cards.position: By nature their twenties side is the original one, a bit of a loner with ideas of its own, black sheep or rebel (13/4). The emotional response under it is fire: push on, and be hard on themselves (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both stand alone and bow to nobody: 13/4 the outsider (13/4), 9 the fighter (9).

course.about: a 4 in the twenties aura (13/4 is the 4 with the ego in it), beside a 9 emotion center
course.text: "There could also have been a tendency in the twenties to be very self-critical (the 9 psychic solar plexus number)."

reasoning: By nature they meet the world as the one who does it differently (13/4), and drive themselves hard to prove the different way works (9).
The combo guide says a hard number such as 9 makes 13/4 rebellious, the dangerous contrarian.
They would rather be right alone (13/4) than give way (9).
cards.best: Tears down what does not work (13/4) and builds its replacement by sheer effort (9).
cards.worst: Opposes something because everyone else supports it (13/4), and makes a fight of it (9).

cards.position: By nature the child in them is lively, likeable and quick, friends with everyone, interested in everything (14/5). The emotional response that goes with it is fire: push on, and be hard on themselves (9).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 14/5 scatters its attention (14/5). 9 wants one thing done properly (9).

course.text: "You probably didn't go into super much depth about any one thing, preferring to generalise your attention."

reasoning: By nature they start many things (14/5), and hold it against themselves that few are finished (9).
The friendly talker (14/5) has a temper under it that friends meet late (9).
The owner's phrase for 5 with 9 is "direct communication": a quick tongue (14/5) with a fighter behind it (9).
cards.best: Gets everyone talking (14/5) and then gets them moving (9).
cards.worst: Laughs it off in company (14/5) and tears into themselves alone (9).

cards.position: In their twenties they had charm and turned heads; it was the time they drew a partner (6). The emotional response under it is attraction with the ego in it: wanting to be wanted, temptation, and drama (15/6).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are sixes: love and attraction (6, 15/6). 15/6 is the 6 that makes drama. The theme is doubled.

course.text: "it's likely that you met your current spouse during this period, as it marks the peak of sexual charisma."

reasoning: In their twenties attention came without effort (6), and they found they needed it (15/6).
The 6 wanted to settle with one partner (6). The 15/6 under it wanted to stay desired by many (15/6).
Nothing in this pair sets a limit (6, 15/6), so love life in the twenties was likely full and stormy.
cards.best: Charmed people in their twenties (6) and loved wholeheartedly (15/6).
cards.worst: Had a devoted partner (6) and still went looking to be wanted (15/6).

cards.position: As a child they were a fighter: fair, direct, and guarded about showing feeling (9). In their twenties they had charm and turned heads; it was the time they drew a partner (6).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 9 keeps people off (9). 6 draws them in (6).

course.about: a 9 childhood aura with sixes beside it
course.text: "Here, the fighting spirit acquired as a child combines with the lessons of love encountered in life to create a strong matriarchal or patriarchal energy."

reasoning: The child would not be hugged (9). In their twenties they discovered they liked being liked (6).
The same passage calls love their biggest lesson: learning to care for people (6) after a childhood of standing guard (9).
Their charm has backbone in it (9): they are warm (6), and nobody takes them for a pushover.
cards.best: Fought for siblings as a child (9) and built a loving family as an adult (6).
cards.worst: Wins a partner's heart (6) and then keeps them at arm's length (9).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 15/6, charm and wanting to be wanted.

phrases: The Little Leader With a Big Heart
cards.position: By nature the child in them is strong in body and mind, divides opinion, and defends itself by being the best at something (10/1). The emotional response that goes with it is loving and wants harmony (6).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are warm, well-liked numbers (10/1, 6), and 10/1 turns the love up (6).

course.text: "You have a great ability to create peace and love in the environment due to a great inner sense of what is right and wrong."

reasoning: By nature they want to be first (10/1), and they want everyone to be happy about it (6).
The child's pride (10/1) is softened by a real wish to look after people (6).
Being disliked is their sore point: the 10/1 splits a room (10/1), and the 6 cannot bear a split (6).
cards.best: Leads with confidence (10/1) and with love for the people led (6).
cards.worst: Has to be the favorite (10/1) and charms everyone to make sure (6).

phrases: Covers the Soft Spot by Winning
cards.position: By nature the child in them is very sensitive: easily hurt, unable to defend itself, hiding in a world of its own (11/2). By nature their twenties side is strong and sure, the one who shows they are the best (10/1).

course.text: "In your twenties, you might well have tried to cover up any weaknesses by displaying a strong winning mentality."

reasoning: The twenties side wins (10/1) so that nobody sees the child who cried easily (11/2).
10/1 turns up what stands beside it (10/1), so the sensitivity is stronger, not weaker, for being covered (11/2).
On the off days of 10/1 (10/1), the child's wish to hide comes straight back (11/2).
cards.best: Feels deeply (11/2) and has the confidence to show it (10/1).
cards.worst: Boasts (10/1) to cover how easily they are hurt (11/2).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 3, talking a feeling out and making a plan of it.
